levels.name: Daisy, 22, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of lying on your resume about Excel. Level 1. Level 1: 1% Proficiency in Excel – and I just deleted the entire company database with one single click. I am Daisy, 22, intern, and my glowing forehead badge says one percent while I sweat over a laptop that cost more than my rent. I only wrote advanced pivot tables to get my foot in the door at the downtown marketing firm. You call this advanced data sorting, Daisy? You don't even know how to freeze panes. The entire quarterly revenue sheet just vanished into thin air. Security is already on floor three. Pack your tiny desk plant right now. Can I somehow recover the lost file before security shows up at my desk? You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Leo, 25, Junior Analyst
levels.story: The 8 levels of lying on your resume about Excel. Level 2. Level 2: 15% Proficiency in Excel – and my boss just found my secret Google search history for VLOOKUP tutorials. I am Leo, 25, junior analyst, an orange person with bright citrus skin wearing a slightly stained polyester tie in cubicle four. My forehead glows with a fifteen percent rating, and today is the day of the annual audit. Is this a joke, Leo? You wrote master of macros on your CV, but you cannot even write a basic sum formula without an error message. My throat went completely dry while the office watched my humiliating public exposure. Just hand over the badge and leave your security pass on the keyboard, kid. Could my hidden macro file save my job at the very last second? You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Marcus, 31, Senior Clerk
levels.story: The 8 levels of lying on your resume about Excel. Level 3. Level 3: 45% Proficiency in Excel – and I just realized my entire department uses formulas I copied from Reddit five years ago. I am Marcus, 31, senior clerk, a strict broccoli person in a fitted charcoal suit. My forehead shows forty-five percent, and I thought I was untouchable until Elena walked into my office with a smirk. You call this data modeling, Marcus? A high schooler with a calculator does better financial forecasting than this mess. My ears burned red while the junior staff pretended not to hear the public dressing down. The regional director is CC'd on the audit email. You better have a good explanation. Was the spreadsheet model I stole from my old roommate actually worth millions? You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Viktor, 39, VP of Analytics
levels.story: The 8 levels of lying on your resume about Excel. Level 6. Level 6: 85% Proficiency in Excel – and I just discovered someone else wrote the VBA code that made me a multi-millionaire.
